newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Sierra Leone rebel chief says coup no surprise.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rebel chief says coup no surprise.

text.p: Sierra Leonean rebel leader Foday Sankoh said on Sunday he was not surprised by an early morning army coup that toppled President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
"It is too early to comment. I can't say I am happy but I'm not surprised," Sankoh, the leader of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF), told Reuters from the Nigerian capital Abuja.
"I was not informed by man of this coup but I had a vision from the Almighty a few days ago that something was about to happen in Sierra Leone," he added.
Sankoh has been kept in a luxury hotel suit for the past two months in Abuja by Nigeria's military authorities.

He denies he is being detained and says his mission to Nigeria is to see military ruler General Sani Abacha to seek his contribution, as chairman of the Economic Community of West African States, to the Sierra Leone peace process.
He has so far not been received by Abacha or any senior Nigerian government official although he said he expected to meet Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi later this week.

In Freetown, Coporal Gborie, who identified himself as the spokesman of the soldiers who toppled Kabbah, called for the return of Sankoh and Captain Solomon Musa, a former deputy leader linked to coup allegations in 1993.
"These are men I brought up in the army," Sankoh said of Gborie and his colleagues.

Ten days ago, Sankoh said he wanted to return home to put on track the peace treaty he had signed with Kabbah's government, saying the authorities there were mistaken in believing that there could be peace by keeping him out of Sierra Leone.
"By the will of the Almighty I should be in Sierra Leone soon," he said on Sunday.
Nigeria has so far made no comment on his stay in the country nor was there any immediate comment from Abuja on the latest coup in Sierra Leone.
Sankoh's RUF has fought Sierra Leone troops in a civil war that began in 1991 and has killed at least 10,000.
Nigerian troops played a supporting role to the Sierra Leone army, stationing a battalion of troops in Freetown.

The leadership of the RUF was thrown into confusion in March when one faction outside Sierra Leone said it had deposed Sankoh. But when officials of the group tried to return home, they were held by Sankoh loyalists in Sierra Leone.
